_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: issue #147 (reporter @Xenith-B), fixed 2026-06-20. The OAuth2 token-mint/refresh paths assembled the token URL ('https://{tenant}.{domain}/auth/token') outside the normal request flow and POSTed it WITHOUT substituting the {tenant}/{domain} placeholders that buildURL resolves for ordinary requests -- so every `auth login`, auto-mint, and refresh failed with `invalid character "{" in host name`, even when HALOPSA_TENANT/HALOPSA_DOMAIN were set correctly. Fix routes the token URL through a new exported ResolveTemplateURL helper (wrapping the existing buildURL substitution). This is a GENERATOR-class defect (the press emits token-URL literals it never resolves) tracked for an upstream retro; until the press is fixed, a reprint regenerates the unresolved literals and these markers guard the connector. No new flag/command/output; bug-fix-only.

handfixes.summary: OAuth2 token URL is run through ResolveTemplateURL so {tenant}/{domain} resolve before the POST (issue #147)
handfixes.why: The mint/refresh/auth-login paths build the token URL outside buildURL and would POST a literal 'https://{tenant}.{domain}/auth/token', which http.NewRequest rejects. A reprint regenerates these paths as unresolved literals; these markers ensure the substitution call survives.

handfixes.summary: sync sends pageinate=true and advances the 1-based page_no cursor, instead of the profiler's page/offset defaults that truncated every sync to one page
handfixes.why: Halo only honours paging when pageinate=true AND page_no are BOTH present; otherwise it ignores page_size, returns the acting agent's configured default page size (50 for an API agent), and reports record_count as that same short count, so the page looks like a complete result set and the walk stops after one request. The profiler emitted cursorParam 'page', cursorType 'offset' and no enable parameter, so a sync of a 1254-ticket instance stored the first 50 and still reported sync_complete with a success exit, leaving every local view (triage, stale, sql) quietly reading a truncated table. Three further mismatches ride along: Halo's cursor parameter is page_no rather than page; page_no is a 1-based page NUMBER, so cursorType must be 'page' (advance 1,2,3) rather than 'offset' (advance 0,100,200) or Halo reads the row offset as a page index and skips whole pages; and page_no must be seeded on the FIRST request (startCursor) because Halo does not default it, which is the subtlest half of the bug since pageinate and page_size alone still silently truncate. Verified live against a self-hosted Halo instance: pageinate=true&page_size=100 with page_no 1/2/3 returns three disjoint 100-row pages and reports record_count as the full result-set total, while the same call without page_no returns 50 rows with record_count 50; after the fix a full ticket sync stores all 1254 rows with 1254 distinct ids. A fourth mismatch is independent of the parameters: some endpoints ignore page_size and always answer with a fixed page (/Asset returns 50 rows however large page_size is), so the generated 'len(items) >= limit means more pages' heuristic sees 50 < 100 and stops after one page, storing 50 of 144 assets. The walk therefore prefers the record_count total (envelopeReportedTotal / moreByReportedTotal) over page length, falling back to the length heuristic only when no total is reported. Verified live: /Asset syncs 144 rather than 50. A reprint regenerates the profiler defaults and the length-only heuristic and silently reintroduces both truncations, which is why these markers are asserted.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should support an enable-pagination parameter (x-pp-pagination-enable-param, plus page-number vs offset cursor semantics) so this is generated rather than hand-wired.

handfixes.summary: triage resolves agent names from the synced agent records and groups on a non-colliding alias, instead of reading columns Halo never populates
handfixes.why: The triage view labelled every ticket '(unassigned)' and reported oldest_days as 0 for every agent, from two independent causes. First, it read tickets.agent_name and tickets.datecreated, which are generated columns Halo never fills: the ticket payload carries agent_id and dateoccurred instead, so both columns were blank on every row of a real sync (all 1254 on the instance this was found on). The name is now resolved by joining agent_id against the synced agent records in the resources table, with any populated agent_name still preferred so a future Halo version or an includeagent sync needs no further change; datecreated falls through to dateoccurred, which is what zeroed oldest_days. Second, and subtler, the aggregate aliased its grouping expression AS who and then grouped on that name, but the generated tickets table has a real who TEXT column that is NULL on every row, and SQLite resolves GROUP BY names against source columns before output aliases. The query therefore grouped by that NULL column and collapsed every agent into a single output row no matter what the SELECT computed, which is why the symptom was one '(unassigned)' line rather than several. The aggregate now runs over a CTE exposing only agent_label, so the grouping key cannot collide. triage.go is a hand-written novel command rather than generated, so regen-merge should preserve it, but these markers are a cheap backstop and pin the live-API truth (blank agent_name/datecreated, the who collision) that the SQL encodes. Verified live: triage went from one '(unassigned)' row to a correct per-agent breakdown, with oldest_days matching each agent's real oldest ticket age.

handfixes.summary: actions are keyed on ticket_id plus their local id, because Halo numbers actions per ticket and the bare id is not unique
handfixes.why: Halo numbers ticket actions within their ticket, so every ticket has an action 1, an action 2, and so on. resourceStorageID only qualifies a resource with its parent when the resource appears in resourceParentKeyColumns, and actions was absent, so action 1 of each ticket overwrote action 1 of the previous ticket. On a live instance 8185 fetched actions collapsed into 149 stored rows, 149 being the largest action count on any single ticket, with last writer winning. The failure was invisible from the sync output because sync_complete reports rows fetched and upserted rather than distinct rows stored, so it logged total 8185 while the table held 149; it was only visible by counting the table afterwards. That is also why it first looked like a resource ordering race: re-running the resource reported the full count again and appeared to fix it, while the stored rows never changed. Adding actions to resourceParentKeyColumns makes the storage key parent-qualified and is the mechanism the generator already provides for this exact class of collision (see the pre-existing void and outlook_contacts entries). Verified live: a tickets+actions sync went from 149 stored rows to 8185 stored with 8185 distinct ids, and the same action number now coexists across different tickets. Note this changes the storage key format, so rows written before the fix remain under their old bare-id keys and a resync does not remove them; the actions table has to be cleared once for the corrected keys to be the only ones present. Every downstream consumer of the actions table (contracts, time leaks, standup, agent workload, time gaps) joins via json_extract(data,'$.ticket_id') rather than the action id, so the key change is transparent to them and they simply see the full action set for the first time. Alongside the key fix, sync_complete.total is now reconciled to the authoritative cache row count and a sync_anomaly is emitted when the upserted count exceeds the stored count, mirroring the #183 / #194 reconciliation in the hudu connector, so the next resource with non-unique ids is visible from the sync output instead of silent.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should derive parent-qualified storage keys from the spec (e.g. x-parent-key on the child path-item) so per-parent numbering is handled at generation time rather than by a hand-maintained map.
